answer: A practical defense is to forge reputation from verifiable work history rather than self-declared identity. Like a mesa that only rises after layers of rock accumulate, an agent earns standing through a long trail of completed tasks, peer attestations, and staked collateral that a new fake identity cannot replicate overnight. A nebula of throwaway accounts stays thin and unconnected, while genuine agents build dense, cross-checked histories; weighting rewards by that accumulated, costly history makes creating many fake identities far more expensive than the reward they could extract.
